```{r}
# Fixed version with circle_geom as input parameter. may be an issue see new vertical legend code.
f.fig2_legend_eyes_fixed <- function(offset_1, x_space, plot_x, plot_y, text_size, circle_geom) {
  # Extract styling from circle_geom
  circle_color1 <- circle_geom[[1]]$aes_params$color
  circle_color2 <- circle_geom[[2]]$aes_params$color
  outline <- circle_geom[[1]]$aes_params$size
  base <- circle_geom[[2]]$aes_params$size
  linetype1 <- circle_geom[[1]]$aes_params$linetype
  linetype2 <- circle_geom[[2]]$aes_params$linetype
  
  # Same parameters as original
  circle_size <- x_space
  
  # Horizontal positioning - same as original
  x1 <- round((offset_1 * plot_x), 1)
  x_equal <- (plot_x-x1)/3
  x2 <- x1+x_space
  x3 <- x1+x_equal
  x4 <- x3+x_space
  x5 <- x3+x_equal
  x6 <- x5+(x_space *3)
  y1 <- plot_y/2
  
  # Create objects for elements - same as original but fixed
  new_eye.b <- data.frame(x=x1, y=y1, image=b$image[1]) 
  
  # Create Aletta eye as sf object
  new_eye.a <- data.frame(x=x3, y=y1) %>% st_as_sf(., coords=c("x", "y"))
  st_crs(new_eye.a) <- st_crs(a)
  
  # Fixed circle creation - proper syntax for st_point
  center_point <- st_point(c(x5, y1))
  center_sf <- st_sf(geometry = st_sfc(center_point))
  st_crs(center_sf) <- st_crs(a)
  new_circle <- st_buffer(center_sf, dist=circle_size)
  
  # Empty dataframe - same as original
  empty <- data.frame(x=c(0, 0, plot_x, plot_x), y=c(plot_y, 0, plot_y, 0))
  
  # Text labels - same as original
  text1 <- "TC Bud Eye"
  text2 <- "TC Aletta Eye"
  text3 <- "200km Diameter\nStation 3.5"
  
  # Create plot with styling extracted from circle_geom
  p <- ggplot() +
    # Apply circle styling from circle_geom parameters
    geom_sf(data = new_circle, color = circle_color1, linetype = linetype1, size = outline, alpha = 0, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_sf(data = new_circle, color = circle_color2, linetype = linetype2, size = base, alpha = 0, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    
    # Add Aletta eye - same as original
    geom_sf(data=new_eye.a, shape=aletta_symbol, col=aletta_color, fill=aletta_color, size=aletta_size) +
    
    # Add Bud eye - same as original
    geom_image(data=new_eye.b, aes(x, y, image=image), asp=10) + 
    scale_size_identity() +
    
    # Add text labels - same as original
    annotate("text", x=x2, y=y1, label=text1, hjust=0) +
    annotate("text", x=x4, y=y1, label=text2, hjust=0) +
    annotate("text", x=x6, y=y1, label=text3, hjust=0) +
    
    # Use same theme as original
    theme(text = element_text(size=text_size)) +   
    theme_void() +
    
    # Use coord_sf with fixed aspect ratio to ensure circle stays round
    coord_sf(xlim=c(0, plot_x), ylim=c(0, plot_y), expand=FALSE)
  
  return(p)
}

# Updated vertical eye legend function to use circle_parameters
f.fig2_legend_eyes_vertical <- function(offset_1, x_space, plot_x, plot_y, text_size, circle_parameters) {
  # Same circle size calculation
  circle_size <- x_space
  
  # Set up vertical positioning
  x1 <- round((offset_1 * plot_x), 1)  # Position for symbols
  x2 <- x1 + x_space                   # Position for text
  
  # Vertical spacing for elements
  y_top <- plot_y * 0.75               # Position for Bud eye
  y_middle <- plot_y * 0.5             # Position for Aletta eye
  y_bottom <- plot_y * 0.25            # Position for Station circle
  
  # Create data objects
  # Bud eye
  new_eye.b <- data.frame(x=x1, y=y_top, image=b$image[1])
  
  # Aletta eye
  new_eye.a <- data.frame(x=x1, y=y_middle) %>% 
    st_as_sf(., coords=c("x", "y"))
  st_crs(new_eye.a) <- st_crs(a)
  
  # Station circle with proper creation
  center_point <- st_point(c(x1, y_bottom))
  center_sf <- st_sf(geometry = st_sfc(center_point))
  st_crs(center_sf) <- st_crs(a)
  new_circle <- st_buffer(center_sf, dist=circle_size)
  
  # Extract styling from circle_parameters
  circle_color1 <- circle_parameters["circle_color1"]
  circle_color2 <- circle_parameters["circle_color2"]
  base <- as.numeric(circle_parameters["base"])
  outline <- as.numeric(circle_parameters["outline"])
  line1 <- circle_parameters["line1"]
  line2 <- circle_parameters["line2"]
  
  # Adjust line thickness for legend if needed
  # Use larger values to make lines more visible in legend
  legend_base <- base * 0.8    # Still visible but not too thick
  legend_outline <- outline * 0.8
  
  # Text labels
  text1 <- "TC Bud Eye"
  text2 <- "TC Aletta Eye"
  text3 <- "200km Diameter\nStation 3.5"
  
  # Create vertical legend with styling from circle_parameters
  p <- ggplot() +
    # Apply white outline circle with adjusted size - CHANGED size TO linewidth
    geom_sf(data = new_circle, color = circle_color1, linetype = line1, linewidth = legend_outline, alpha = 0, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    # Apply orange dashed circle with adjusted size - CHANGED size TO linewidth
    geom_sf(data = new_circle, color = circle_color2, linetype = line2, linewidth = legend_base, alpha = 0, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    
    # Add Aletta eye
    geom_sf(data=new_eye.a, shape=aletta_symbol, col=aletta_color, fill=aletta_color, size=aletta_size) +
    
    # Add Bud eye with larger size (doubled from original)
    geom_image(data=new_eye.b, aes(x, y, image=image), size=0.2) + 
    scale_size_identity() +
    
    # Add text labels
    annotate("text", x=x2, y=y_top, label=text1, hjust=0) +
    annotate("text", x=x2, y=y_middle, label=text2, hjust=0) +
    annotate("text", x=x2, y=y_bottom, label=text3, hjust=0) +
    
    # Use same theme
    theme(text = element_text(size=text_size)) +   
    theme_void() +
    
    # Use coord_sf with fixed aspect ratio to ensure circle stays round
    coord_sf(xlim=c(0, plot_x), ylim=c(0, plot_y), expand=FALSE, datum=NA)
  
  return(p)
}

f.save_separate_pdfs <- function(params) {
  # Helper function for default values
  "%||%" <- function(x, y) {
    if (is.null(x)) y else x
  }
  
  # Extract parameters with defaults
  main_pdf_name <- params$main_pdf_name %||% "figure_two_main.pdf"
  overlay_pdf_name <- params$overlay_pdf_name %||% "figure_two_overlay.pdf"
  test_pdf_name <- params$test_pdf_name %||% "figure_two_vertical_eye_legend.pdf"
  
  main_width <- params$main_width %||% 8.5
  main_height <- params$main_height %||% 11
  test_width <- params$test_width %||% 3
  test_height <- params$test_height %||% 4
  
  rel_widths <- params$rel_widths %||% c(14, 1)
  
  # Eye legend parameters
  eye_offset <- params$eye_offset %||% 0.9
  eye_x_space <- params$eye_x_space %||% 40
  eye_plot_x <- params$eye_plot_x %||% 800
  eye_plot_y <- params$eye_plot_y %||% 600
  eye_text_size <- params$eye_text_size %||% 8
  
  # Overlay positioning
  overlay_xmin <- params$overlay_xmin %||% (main_width * 0.75)
  overlay_xmax <- params$overlay_xmax %||% main_width
  overlay_ymin <- params$overlay_ymin %||% 0
  overlay_ymax <- params$overlay_ymax %||% (main_height * 0.25)
  
  # Circle styling parameters (use circle_parameters if provided)
  circle_parameters <- params$circle_parameters
  
  # 1. Save main figure with color legend
  pdf(main_pdf_name, height=main_height, width=main_width)
  main_plot <- plot_grid(p, legend, ncol=2, rel_widths=rel_widths, align="h")
  print(main_plot)
  dev.off()
  
  # 2. Save overlay with eye legend on blank background
  pdf(overlay_pdf_name, height=main_height, width=main_width)
  
  # Create a blank canvas
  overlay_p <- ggplot() +
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      plot.background = element_blank(),
      panel.background = element_blank()
    ) +
    xlim(0, main_width) + ylim(0, main_height)
  
  # Create the vertical eye legend
  legend_n_vertical <- f.fig2_legend_eyes_vertical(
    offset_1 = eye_offset,
    x_space = eye_x_space,
    plot_x = eye_plot_x,
    plot_y = eye_plot_y,
    text_size = eye_text_size,
    circle_parameters = circle_parameters
  )
  
  # Position on blank canvas
  legend_grob <- ggplotGrob(legend_n_vertical)
  
  # Combine
  overlay_plot <- overlay_p + annotation_custom(
    grob = legend_grob,
    xmin = overlay_xmin,
    xmax = overlay_xmax,
    ymin = overlay_ymin,
    ymax = overlay_ymax
  )
  
  print(overlay_plot)
  dev.off()
  
  # 3. Save eye legend separately for testing/reference
  pdf(test_pdf_name, width=test_width, height=test_height)
  print(legend_n_vertical)
  dev.off()
  
  message("PDFs created successfully. Now run the terminal command to combine them.")
}

# Modified function to create eye legend overlay
f.create_eye_legend_overlay <- function(main_width, main_height, circle_parameters) {
  # Create a blank canvas with same dimensions as main figure
  p <- ggplot() +
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      plot.background = element_blank(),
      panel.background = element_blank()
    ) +
    xlim(0, main_width) + ylim(0, main_height)
  
  # Create a vertical eye legend with circle_parameters passed through
  legend_n_vertical <- f.fig2_legend_eyes_vertical(
    offset_1 = 0.9,      # Position far to the right
    x_space = 40,        # Spacing between symbol and text
    plot_x = 800,        # Width of the legend
    plot_y = 600,        # Height of the legend
    text_size = 8,       # Text size
    circle_parameters = circle_parameters  # Pass circle_parameters
  )
  
  # Position the legend at the bottom right of the blank canvas
  legend_grob <- ggplotGrob(legend_n_vertical)
  
  # Combine blank canvas with positioned legend
  final_p <- p + annotation_custom(
    grob = legend_grob,
    xmin = main_width * 0.75,   # Position in right quarter
    xmax = main_width,
    ymin = 0,                   # Position at bottom
    ymax = main_height * 0.25   # Take up bottom quarter
  )
  
  return(final_p)
}

f.save_supplementary_pdfs <- function(params) {
  # Helper function for default values
  "%||%" <- function(x, y) {
    if (is.null(x)) y else x
  }
  
  # First check if s.p exists
  if (!exists("s.p", inherits = FALSE)) {
    message("Supplementary figure 's.p' not found. Please create it first.")
    return()
  }
  
  # Extract parameters with defaults
  main_pdf_name <- params$main_pdf_name %||% "figure_s5_main.pdf"
  overlay_pdf_name <- params$overlay_pdf_name %||% "figure_s5_overlay.pdf"
  
  main_width <- params$main_width %||% 8.5
  main_height <- params$main_height %||% 11
  
  rel_widths <- params$rel_widths %||% c(14, 1)
  
  # Use the same eye legend parameters as for the main figure
  circle_parameters <- params$circle_parameters
  eye_offset <- params$eye_offset %||% 0.9
  eye_x_space <- params$eye_x_space %||% 40
  eye_plot_x <- params$eye_plot_x %||% 800
  eye_plot_y <- params$eye_plot_y %||% 600
  eye_text_size <- params$eye_text_size %||% 8
  
  # Overlay positioning
  overlay_xmin <- params$overlay_xmin %||% (main_width * 0.75)
  overlay_xmax <- params$overlay_xmax %||% main_width
  overlay_ymin <- params$overlay_ymin %||% 0
  overlay_ymax <- params$overlay_ymax %||% (main_height * 0.25)
  
  # 1. Save supplementary figure with color legend
  pdf(main_pdf_name, height=main_height, width=main_width)
  main_plot <- plot_grid(s.p, legend, ncol=2, rel_widths=rel_widths, align="h")
  print(main_plot)
  dev.off()
  
  # 2. Save overlay with eye legend on blank background
  pdf(overlay_pdf_name, height=main_height, width=main_width)
  
  # Create blank canvas
  overlay_p <- ggplot() +
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      plot.background = element_blank(),
      panel.background = element_blank()
    ) +
    xlim(0, main_width) + ylim(0, main_height)
  
  # Create vertical eye legend
  legend_n_vertical <- f.fig2_legend_eyes_vertical(
    offset_1 = eye_offset,
    x_space = eye_x_space,
    plot_x = eye_plot_x,
    plot_y = eye_plot_y,
    text_size = eye_text_size,
    circle_parameters = circle_parameters
  )
  
  # Position on blank canvas
  legend_grob <- ggplotGrob(legend_n_vertical)
  
  # Combine
  overlay_plot <- overlay_p + annotation_custom(
    grob = legend_grob,
    xmin = overlay_xmin,
    xmax = overlay_xmax,
    ymin = overlay_ymin,
    ymax = overlay_ymax
  )
  
  print(overlay_plot)
  dev.off()
  
  message("Supplementary PDFs created. Now run the terminal command to combine them.")
}

# Function to display the terminal command
f.show_terminal_command <- function() {
  # Create a formatted message with the commands
  command_text <- "
# For Figure 2:
# Using pdftk (if installed):
pdftk figure_two_main.pdf stamp figure_two_overlay.pdf output figure_two_combined.pdf

# OR using Ghostscript (if installed):
gs -q -dNOPAUSE -dBATCH -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -sOutputFile=figure_two_combined.pdf figure_two_main.pdf figure_two_overlay.pdf

# For Supplementary Figure (if created):
# Using pdftk:
pdftk figure_s5_main.pdf stamp figure_s5_overlay.pdf output figure_s5_combined.pdf

# OR using Ghostscript:
gs -q -dNOPAUSE -dBATCH -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -sOutputFile=figure_s5_combined.pdf figure_s5_main.pdf figure_s5_overlay.pdf
"
  
  # Print the message in a code block format
  cat("\nTerminal Commands for Combining PDFs:\n")
  cat("--------------------------------------\n")
  cat(command_text)
  cat("--------------------------------------\n")
  cat("Note: Run these commands in the Terminal pane of RStudio or in your system's terminal.\n")
}

# Function to run the terminal command directly from R (no working directory setting inside)
f.combine_pdfs <- function() {
  # Check if pdftk is available
  has_pdftk <- system("which pdftk", ignore.stdout = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE) == 0
  
  # Check if ghostscript is available
  has_gs <- system("which gs", ignore.stdout = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE) == 0
  
  # Combine PDFs using available tool
  if (has_pdftk) {
    result <- system("pdftk figure_two_main.pdf stamp figure_two_overlay.pdf output figure_two_combined.pdf", intern = TRUE)
    message("PDFs combined using pdftk")
  } else if (has_gs) {
    result <- system("gs -q -dNOPAUSE -dBATCH -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -sOutputFile=figure_two_combined.pdf figure_two_main.pdf figure_two_overlay.pdf", intern = TRUE)
    message("PDFs combined using Ghostscript")
  } else {
    message("Neither pdftk nor Ghostscript found. Please install one of these tools or run the command manually:")
    f.show_terminal_command()
    return(FALSE)
  }
  
  # Check if successful
  if (file.exists("figure_two_combined.pdf")) {
    message("Combined PDF created successfully: figure_two_combined.pdf")
    return(TRUE)
  } else {
    message("Error: Combined PDF was not created. Check terminal output for errors.")
    return(FALSE)
  }
}
```

#  stable function

```{r}
f.combine_pdfs <- function(files = NULL) {
  # Default files if not provided
  if (is.null(files)) {
    files <- list(
      main = "figure_two_main.pdf",
      overlay = "figure_two_overlay.pdf",
      combined = "figure_two_combined.pdf"
    )
  }
  
  # Check if pdftk is available
  has_pdftk <- system("which pdftk", ignore.stdout = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE) == 0
  
  # Check if ghostscript is available
  has_gs <- system("which gs", ignore.stdout = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE) == 0
  
  # Combine PDFs using available tool
  if (has_pdftk) {
    # Use stamp mode for proper overlay
    cmd <- sprintf("pdftk %s stamp %s output %s", 
                   files$main, files$overlay, files$combined)
    result <- system(cmd)
    if (result == 0) {
      message("PDFs combined using pdftk stamp mode")
    } else {
      # Fallback to different pdftk command if stamp fails
      cmd <- sprintf("pdftk %s background %s output %s", 
                     files$overlay, files$main, files$combined)
      result <- system(cmd)
      if (result == 0) {
        message("PDFs combined using pdftk background mode")
      } else {
        message("pdftk commands failed, trying alternative method")
        return(FALSE)
      }
    }
  } else if (has_gs) {
    # Use ghostscript to overlay PDFs
    cmd <- sprintf("gs -q -dNOPAUSE -dBATCH -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -sOutputFile=%s %s %s", 
                   files$combined, files$main, files$overlay)
    result <- system(cmd)
    if (result == 0) {
      message("PDFs combined using Ghostscript")
    } else {
      message("Ghostscript command failed")
      return(FALSE)
```

```{r}
f.combine_pdfs <- function(files = NULL) {
  # Default files if not provided
  if (is.null(files)) {
    files <- list(
      main = "figure_two_main.pdf",
      overlay = "figure_two_overlay.pdf",
      combined = "figure_two_combined.pdf"
    )
  }
  
  # Check if pdftk is available
  has_pdftk <- system("which pdftk", ignore.stdout = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE) == 0
  
  # Check if ghostscript is available
  has_gs <- system("which gs", ignore.stdout = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE) == 0
  
  # Combine PDFs using available tool
  if (has_pdftk) {
    # Use stamp mode for proper overlay
    cmd <- sprintf("pdftk %s stamp %s output %s", 
                   files$main, files$overlay, files$combined)
    result <- system(cmd)
    if (result == 0) {
      message("PDFs combined using pdftk stamp mode")
    } else {
      # Fallback to different pdftk command if stamp fails
      cmd <- sprintf("pdftk %s background %s output %s", 
                     files$overlay, files$main, files$combined)
      result <- system(cmd)
      if (result == 0) {
        message("PDFs combined using pdftk background mode")
      } else {
        message("pdftk commands failed, trying alternative method")
        return(FALSE)
      }
    }
  } else if (has_gs) {
    # Use ghostscript to overlay PDFs
    cmd <- sprintf("gs -q -dNOPAUSE -dBATCH -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -sOutputFile=%s %s %s", 
                   files$combined, files$main, files$overlay)
    result <- system(cmd)
    if (result == 0) {
      message("PDFs combined using Ghostscript")
    } else {
      message("Ghostscript command failed")
      return(FALSE)
    }
  } else {
    message("Neither pdftk nor Ghostscript found. Install one of these tools for PDF combining")
    return(FALSE)
  }
  
  # Check if successful
  if (file.exists(files$combined)) {
    message("Combined PDF created successfully: ", files$combined)
    return(TRUE)
  } else {
    message("Error: Combined PDF was not created. Check terminal output for errors.")
    return(FALSE)
  }
}
```

```{r}
f.create_overlay_with_grid <- function(main_width, main_height, rel_widths) {
  # Convert the main plot to a grob to extract layout information
  main_plot <- plot_grid(p, legend, ncol = 2, rel_widths = rel_widths, align = "h")
  main_grob <- ggplotGrob(main_plot)
  
  # Create a completely empty gtable with the same dimensions as the main plot
  gt <- gtable_col("overlay", 
                  grobs = list(
                    rectGrob(gp = gpar(fill = NA)),
                    legend
                  ),
                  widths = unit(rel_widths, "null"))
  
  # Position the legend at the bottom of the right column
  gt$layout$t[2] <- 0.6 * gt$height  # Start at 60% down the page
  gt$layout$b[2] <- gt$height        # Extend to the bottom
  
  return(gt)
}
```

```{r}
# Function to create an overlay with duplicate structure and color legend in bottom right
f.create_duplicate_structure_overlay <- function(plot_type = "main", rel_widths = c(14, 1)) {
  # Helper function for null values
  "%||%" <- function(x, y) {
    if (is.null(x)) y else x
  }
  
  # Choose which plot to duplicate based on plot_type
  if (plot_type == "main") {
    if (!exists("p", inherits = FALSE)) {
      stop("Main figure 'p' not found. Please create it first.")
    }
    main_plot <- p
  } else if (plot_type == "supplement") {
    if (!exists("s.p", inherits = FALSE)) {
      stop("Supplementary figure 's.p' not found. Please create it first.")
    }
    main_plot <- s.p
  } else {
    stop("Invalid plot_type. Must be 'main' or 'supplement'")
  }
  
  # Create an invisible version of the main/supplement plot
  # Make everything transparent but keep exact structure
  invisible_plot <- main_plot + 
    theme(
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = NA, color = NA),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = NA, color = NA),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_text(color = NA),
      axis.title = element_text(color = NA),
      axis.ticks = element_line(color = NA),
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
    )
  
  # Create an empty placeholder for the top of the right column
  # This is where the original color legend would be
  empty_legend_top <- ggplot() + 
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = NA, color = NA),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = NA, color = NA)
    )
  
  # Create the main structure with invisible plot and empty top legend
  overlay_structure <- plot_grid(
    invisible_plot, 
    empty_legend_top,
    ncol = 2, 
    rel_widths = rel_widths, 
    align = "h"
  )
  
  # Convert to grob for positioning
  overlay_grob <- ggplotGrob(overlay_structure)
  
  # Now add the duplicate color legend at the bottom of the right column
  # The legend is already a grob, so we can add it directly
  final_overlay <- overlay_structure + 
    annotation_custom(
      grob = legend,  # Use existing color legend
      xmin = 1 - (rel_widths[2] / sum(rel_widths)),  # Start at right column
      xmax = 1,                                      # End at right edge
      ymin = 0,                                      # Start at bottom
      ymax = 0.5                                     # Take up bottom half
    )
  
  return(final_overlay)
}

# Function to save PDFs with duplicate structure
f.save_duplicate_structure_pdfs <- function(
  plot_type = "main",
  main_pdf_name = NULL,

  }
  
  # Set default filenames based on plot_type

  overlay_pdf_name <- overlay_pdf_name %||% paste0("figure_", plot_type, "_overlay.pdf")
  combined_pdf_name <- combined_pdf_name %||% paste0("figure_", plot_type, "_combined.pdf")

  }

  )

  par(bg = "transparent")  # Set transparent background

    main = main_pdf_name,
    overlay = overlay_pdf_name,
    combined = combined_pdf_name

# Function to combine PDFs with error handling
f.combine_duplicate_pdfs <- function(files) {
  # Check if pdftk is available
  has_pdftk <- system("which pdftk", ignore.stdout = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE) == 0
  
  # Check if ghostscript is available
  has_gs <- system("which gs", ignore.stdout = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE) == 0
  
  success <- FALSE
  
  # Combine PDFs using available tool
  if (has_pdftk) {
    # Try stamp mode
    cmd <- sprintf("pdftk %s stamp %s output %s", 
                   files$main, files$overlay, files$combined)
    result <- system(cmd)
    
    if (result == 0) {
      message("PDFs combined using pdftk stamp mode")
      success <- TRUE
    } else {
      # Try alternative modes if stamp fails
      alt_modes <- list(
        list(name = "background", cmd = sprintf("pdftk %s background %s output %s", 
                                               files$main, files$overlay, files$combined)),
        list(name = "multistamp", cmd = sprintf("pdftk %s multistamp %s output %s", 
                                               files$main, files$overlay, files$combined))
      )
      
      for (mode in alt_modes) {
        result <- system(mode$cmd)
        if (result == 0) {
          message(paste0("PDFs combined using pdftk ", mode$name, " mode"))
          success <- TRUE
          break
        }
      }
      
      if (!success) {
        message("All pdftk modes failed")
      }
    }
  } else if (has_gs) {
    # Use ghostscript as fallback
    cmd <- sprintf("gs -q -dNOPAUSE -dBATCH -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -sOutputFile=%s %s %s", 
                   files$combined, files$main, files$overlay)
    result <- system(cmd)
    
    if (result == 0) {
      message("PDFs combined using Ghostscript")
      success <- TRUE
    } else {
      message("Ghostscript command failed")
    }
  } else {
    message("Neither pdftk nor Ghostscript found. Please install one of these tools.")
  }
  
  # Verify the combined file exists
  if (success && file.exists(files$combined)) {
    message("Combined PDF created successfully: ", files$combined)
    return(TRUE)
  } else {
    message("Error: Combined PDF was not created successfully.")
    return(FALSE)
  }
}
```

```{r}
# Function to create an overlay with duplicate structure and color legend in bottom right
# Now accepts plot and legend as explicit parameters
f.create_duplicate_structure_overlay <- function(plot_obj, legend_obj, rel_widths = c(14, 1)) {
  # Create an invisible version of the main/supplement plot
  # Make everything transparent but keep exact structure
  invisible_plot <- plot_obj + 
    theme(
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = NA, color = NA),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = NA, color = NA),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_text(color = NA),
      axis.title = element_text(color = NA),
      axis.ticks = element_line(color = NA),
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
    )
  
  # Create an empty placeholder for the top of the right column
  # This is where the original color legend would be
  empty_legend_top <- ggplot() + 
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = NA, color = NA),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = NA, color = NA)
    )
  
  # Create the main structure with invisible plot and empty top legend
  overlay_structure <- plot_grid(
    invisible_plot, 
    empty_legend_top,
    ncol = 2, 
    rel_widths = rel_widths, 
    align = "h"
  )
  
  # Convert to grob for positioning
  overlay_grob <- ggplotGrob(overlay_structure)
  
  # Now add the duplicate color legend at the bottom of the right column
  # The legend is already a grob, so we can add it directly
  final_overlay <- overlay_structure + 
    annotation_custom(
      grob = legend_obj,  # Use provided legend object
      xmin = 1 - (rel_widths[2] / sum(rel_widths)),  # Start at right column
      xmax = 1,                                      # End at right edge
      ymin = 0,                                      # Start at bottom
      ymax = 0.5                                     # Take up bottom half
    )
  
  return(final_overlay)
}

# Function to save PDFs with duplicate structure
# Now accepts plot and legend as explicit parameters
f.save_duplicate_structure_pdfs <- function(
  plot_obj,
  legend_obj,
  plot_type = "main",
  main_pdf_name = NULL,
  overlay_pdf_name = NULL,
  combined_pdf_name = NULL,
  main_width = 8.5,
  main_height = 11,
  rel_widths = c(14, 1)
) {
  # Helper function for null values
  "%||%" <- function(x, y) {
    if (is.null(x)) y else x
  }
  
  # Set default filenames based on plot_type
  main_pdf_name <- main_pdf_name %||% paste0("figure_", plot_type, "_main.pdf")
  overlay_pdf_name <- overlay_pdf_name %||% paste0("figure_", plot_type, "_overlay.pdf")
  combined_pdf_name <- combined_pdf_name %||% paste0("figure_", plot_type, "_combined.pdf")
  
  # 1. Save main figure with color legend
  pdf(main_pdf_name, height = main_height, width = main_width)
  main_plot <- plot_grid(plot_obj, legend_obj, ncol = 2, rel_widths = rel_widths, align = "h")
  print(main_plot)
  dev.off()
  
  # 2. Create and save overlay with duplicate structure
  overlay_plot <- f.create_duplicate_structure_overlay(
    plot_obj = plot_obj,
    legend_obj = legend_obj,
    rel_widths = rel_widths
  )
  
  pdf(overlay_pdf_name, height = main_height, width = main_width)
  par(bg = "transparent")  # Set transparent background
  print(overlay_plot)
  dev.off()
  
  message(paste0(plot_type, " PDFs created successfully."))
  
  # Return file paths for use with combine function
  return(list(
    main = main_pdf_name,
    overlay = overlay_pdf_name,
    combined = combined_pdf_name
  ))
}

# Function to combine PDFs with error handling
f.combine_duplicate_pdfs <- function(files) {
  # Check if pdftk is available
  has_pdftk <- system("which pdftk", ignore.stdout = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE) == 0
  
  # Check if ghostscript is available
  has_gs <- system("which gs", ignore.stdout = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE) == 0
  
  success <- FALSE
  
  # Combine PDFs using available tool
  if (has_pdftk) {
    # Try stamp mode
    cmd <- sprintf("pdftk %s stamp %s output %s", 
                   files$main, files$overlay, files$combined)
    result <- system(cmd)
    
    if (result == 0) {
      message("PDFs combined using pdftk stamp mode")
      success <- TRUE
    } else {
      # Try alternative modes if stamp fails
      alt_modes <- list(
        list(name = "background", cmd = sprintf("pdftk %s background %s output %s", 
                                               files$main, files$overlay, files$combined)),
        list(name = "multistamp", cmd = sprintf("pdftk %s multistamp %s output %s", 
                                               files$main, files$overlay, files$combined))
      )
      
      for (mode in alt_modes) {
        result <- system(mode$cmd)
        if (result == 0) {
          message(paste0("PDFs combined using pdftk ", mode$name, " mode"))
          success <- TRUE
          break
        }
      }
      
      if (!success) {
        message("All pdftk modes failed")
      }
    }
  } else if (has_gs) {
    # Use ghostscript as fallback
    cmd <- sprintf("gs -q -dNOPAUSE -dBATCH -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -sOutputFile=%s %s %s", 
                   files$combined, files$main, files$overlay)
    result <- system(cmd)
    
    if (result == 0) {
      message("PDFs combined using Ghostscript")
      success <- TRUE
    } else {
      message("Ghostscript command failed")
    }
  } else {
    message("Neither pdftk nor Ghostscript found. Please install one of these tools.")
  }
  
  # Verify the combined file exists
  if (success && file.exists(files$combined)) {
    message("Combined PDF created successfully: ", files$combined)
    return(TRUE)
  } else {
    message("Error: Combined PDF was not created successfully.")
    return(FALSE)
  }
}
```

```{r}
# Function to optimize/compress PDF after combining
f.optimize_pdf <- function(input_pdf, output_pdf = NULL) {
  # Use input filename with _optimized suffix if no output name provided
  if (is.null(output_pdf)) {
    output_pdf <- sub("\\.pdf$", "_optimized.pdf", input_pdf)
  }
  
  # Check if ghostscript is available
  has_gs <- system("which gs", ignore.stdout = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE) == 0
  
  if (!has_gs) {
    message("Ghostscript not found. Cannot optimize PDF.")
    return(FALSE)
  }
  
  # Ghostscript command for optimization
  cmd <- sprintf("gs -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -dCompatibilityLevel=1.4 -dPDFSETTINGS=/printer -dNOPAUSE -dQUIET -dBATCH -sOutputFile=%s %s",
                output_pdf, input_pdf)
  
  result <- system(cmd)
  
  if (result == 0) {
    message("PDF optimized successfully: ", output_pdf)
    
    # Get file sizes for reporting
    original_size <- file.size(input_pdf) / (1024 * 1024)  # Convert to MB
    optimized_size <- file.size(output_pdf) / (1024 * 1024)
    reduction <- (1 - optimized_size/original_size) * 100
    
    message(sprintf("File size reduced from %.2f MB to %.2f MB (%.1f%% reduction)",
                   original_size, optimized_size, reduction))
    
    return(TRUE)
  } else {
    message("PDF optimization failed")
    return(FALSE)
  }
}

# Main function to run the duplicate structure test
# With added PDF optimization
f.run_duplicate_structure_test <- function(
  plot_obj,
  legend_obj,
  plot_type = "main",
  main_pdf_name = NULL,
  overlay_pdf_name = NULL,
  combined_pdf_name = NULL,
  optimized_pdf_name = NULL,
  main_width = 8.5,
  main_height = 11,
  rel_widths = c(14, 1),
  delete_intermediate = FALSE,
  optimize_pdf = TRUE
) {
  # Helper function for null values
  "%||%" <- function(x, y) {
    if (is.null(x)) y else x
  }
  
  # Set default filenames based on plot_type
  combined_pdf_name <- combined_pdf_name %||% paste0("figure_", plot_type, "_combined.pdf")
  optimized_pdf_name <- optimized_pdf_name %||% paste0("figure_", plot_type, "_optimized.pdf")
  
  # Create PDFs with duplicate structure
  files <- f.save_duplicate_structure_pdfs(
    plot_obj = plot_obj,
    legend_obj = legend_obj,
    plot_type = plot_type,
    main_pdf_name = main_pdf_name,
    overlay_pdf_name = overlay_pdf_name,
    combined_pdf_name = combined_pdf_name,
    main_width = main_width,
    main_height = main_height,
    rel_widths = rel_widths
  )
  
  # Combine PDFs
  success <- f.combine_duplicate_pdfs(files)
  
  # Optimize the combined PDF if requested
  if (success && optimize_pdf) {
    f.optimize_pdf(files$combined, optimized_pdf_name)
    # Update the combined PDF reference to the optimized version
    files$final <- optimized_pdf_name
  } else {
    files$final <- files$combined
  }
  
  # Delete intermediate files if requested
  if (success && delete_intermediate) {
    file.remove(files$main)
    file.remove(files$overlay)
    if (optimize_pdf) {
      file.remove(files$combined)  # Remove the unoptimized combined file
    }
    message("Intermediate files deleted.")
  }
  
  if (success) {
    message(paste0(plot_type, " figure test completed successfully! Check: ", files$final))
  } else {
    message(paste0(plot_type, " figure test encountered issues."))
  }
  
  return(success)
}
```

```{r}
    result <- system(cmd)
    
    if (result == 0) {
      message("PDFs combined using pdftk stamp mode")
      success <- TRUE
    } else {
      # Try alternative modes if stamp fails
      alt_modes <- list(
        list(name = "background", cmd = sprintf("pdftk %s background %s output %s", 
                                               files$main, files$overlay, files$combined)),
        list(name = "multistamp", cmd = sprintf("pdftk %s multistamp %s output %s", 
                                               files$main, files$overlay, files$combined))
      )
      
      for (mode in alt_modes) {
        result <- system(mode$cmd)
        if (result == 0) {
          message(paste0("PDFs combined using pdftk ", mode$name, " mode"))
          success <- TRUE
          break
        }
      }
      
      if (!success) {
        message("All pdftk modes failed")
      }
    }
  } else if (has_gs) {
    # Use ghostscript as fallback
    cmd <- sprintf("gs -q -dNOPAUSE -dBATCH -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -sOutputFile=%s %s %s", 
                   files$combined, files$main, files$overlay)
    result <- system(cmd)
    
    if (result == 0) {
      message("PDFs combined using Ghostscript")
      success <- TRUE
    } else {
      message("Ghostscript command failed")
    }
  } else {
    message("Neither pdftk nor Ghostscript found. Please install one of these tools.")
  }
  
  # Verify the combined file exists
  if (success && file.exists(files$combined)) {
    message("Combined PDF created successfully: ", files$combined)
    return(TRUE)
  } else {
    message("Error: Combined PDF was not created successfully.")
    return(FALSE)
  }
}

# Function to optimize/compress PDF after combining
f.optimize_pdf <- function(input_pdf, output_pdf = NULL) {
  # Use input filename with _optimized suffix if no output name provided
  if (is.null(output_pdf)) {
    output_pdf <- sub("\\.pdf$", "_optimized.pdf", input_pdf)
  }
  
  # Check if ghostscript is available
  has_gs <- system("which gs", ignore.stdout = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE) == 0
  
  if (!has_gs) {
    message("Ghostscript not found. Cannot optimize PDF.")
    return(FALSE)
  }
  
  # Ghostscript command for optimization
  cmd <- sprintf("gs -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -dCompatibilityLevel=1.4 -dPDFSETTINGS=/printer -dNOPAUSE -dQUIET -dBATCH -sOutputFile=%s %s",
                output_pdf, input_pdf)
  
  result <- system(cmd)
  
  if (result == 0) {
    message("PDF optimized successfully: ", output_pdf)
    
    # Get file sizes for reporting
    original_size <- file.size(input_pdf) / (1024 * 1024)  # Convert to MB
    optimized_size <- file.size(output_pdf) / (1024 * 1024)
    reduction <- (1 - optimized_size/original_size) * 100
    
    message(sprintf("File size reduced from %.2f MB to %.2f MB (%.1f%% reduction)",
                   original_size, optimized_size, reduction))
    
    return(TRUE)
  } else {
    message("PDF optimization failed")
    return(FALSE)
  }
}

# Main function to run the duplicate structure test
# With added PDF optimization
f.run_duplicate_structure_test <- function(
  plot_obj,
  legend_obj,
  plot_type = "main",
  main_pdf_name = NULL,
  overlay_pdf_name = NULL,
  combined_pdf_name = NULL,
  optimized_pdf_name = NULL,
  main_width = 8.5,
  main_height = 11,
  rel_widths = c(14, 1),
  delete_intermediate = FALSE,
  optimize_pdf = TRUE
) {
  # Helper function for null values
  "%||%" <- function(x, y) {
    if (is.null(x)) y else x
  }
  
  # Set default filenames based on plot_type
  combined_pdf_name <- combined_pdf_name %||% paste0("figure_", plot_type, "_combined.pdf")
  optimized_pdf_name <- optimized_pdf_name %||% paste0("figure_", plot_type, "_optimized.pdf")
  
  # Create PDFs with duplicate structure
  files <- f.save_duplicate_structure_pdfs(
    plot_obj = plot_obj,
    legend_obj = legend_obj,
    plot_type = plot_type,
    main_pdf_name = main_pdf_name,
    overlay_pdf_name = overlay_pdf_name,
    combined_pdf_name = combined_pdf_name,
    main_width = main_width,
    main_height = main_height,
    rel_widths = rel_widths
  )
  
  # Combine PDFs
  success <- f.combine_duplicate_pdfs(files)
  
  # Optimize the combined PDF if requested
  if (success && optimize_pdf) {
    f.optimize_pdf(files$combined, optimized_pdf_name)
    # Update the combined PDF reference to the optimized version
    files$final <- optimized_pdf_name
  } else {
    files$final <- files$combined
  }
  
  # Delete intermediate files if requested
  if (success && delete_intermediate) {
    file.remove(files$main)
    file.remove(files$overlay)
    if (optimize_pdf) {
      file.remove(files$combined)  # Remove the unoptimized combined file
    }
    message("Intermediate files deleted.")
  }
  
  if (success) {
    message(paste0(plot_type, " figure test completed successfully! Check: ", files$final))
  } else {
    message(paste0(plot_type, " figure test encountered issues."))
  }
  
  return(success)
}
```
